title: Validate mutate_state values before canonical writes
description: Review finding from loreweaver-niw. Runtime validation is missing for typed canonical state fields; SQLite accepts text in numeric columns and invalid JSON strings in JSON columns. Example: hp_current='dead' can persist and later violate TypeScript state contracts. Parent context: loreweaver-d4r.
acceptance_criteria: Invalid numeric, text, and JSON values are rejected with structured tool errors before persistence; regression tests prove hp_current='dead' and quantity='many' do not persist through mutate_state or mutateState.
close_reason: Added field-specific runtime validation before canonical mutate_state writes; invalid numeric/text/JSON values now reject before persistence and tool calls return structured mutate_error. Verification: git diff --check, npm run typecheck, and npm run test passed; TDD evidence recorded.

comments.author: Joseph Bongaarts
comments.text: Debug evidence: mutateState validates target/field/provenance/session/timestamp but setCharacterField, setInventoryField, and setClockField pass input.value directly to SQLite. Root cause hypothesis confirmed from packages/core/src/state/mutateState.ts: field-specific runtime validation is missing before canonical writes.

comments.author: Joseph Bongaarts
comments.text: TDD RED: npm run test -- packages/core/test/gameState.test.ts packages/core/test/tools.test.ts -> failed as expected. gameState invalid hp_current did not throw; mutate_state tool returned ok=true for hp_current='dead'.

comments.author: Joseph Bongaarts
comments.text: TDD GREEN: npm run test -- packages/core/test/gameState.test.ts packages/core/test/tools.test.ts -> passed; 2 files, 27 tests. Invalid hp_current and quantity now reject before persistence; mutate_state returns structured mutate_error.

comments.author: Joseph Bongaarts
comments.text: Verification: git diff --check -> exit 0. npm run typecheck -> exit 0. npm run test -> exit 0; 35 test files passed, 197 tests passed, 1 skipped. TDD evidence: RED focused tests failed for missing validation; GREEN focused tests passed after field-specific validators.
